items.title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
items.summary: We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding.To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that retains BF16 lvl performance on long-horizon agentic tasks.Benchmarks (BF16 / 3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit):- DeepSWE: 39.8 / 41.0 / 41.9 / 28.6- Terminal-Bench 2.1: 62.6 / 63.8 / 60.2 / 52.4- AIME 25+26: 97.7 / 98.3 / 96.5 / 86.0- MSGM: 94.0 / 93.1 / 91.8 / 90.6- RealW

items.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
items.summary:
Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS.
